M123R-01.title: rescue_cleanup()'s own internal steps are not uniformly defensive against unexpected exceptions
M123R-01.reproduction: A NovelBug-type exception raised by referencing_sessions() crashes rescue_cleanup() on its own first loop step; confirmed schema AND run_root both still present immediately after cleanup_run() raises, before any manual teardown -- zero cleanup attempted despite the DROP DATABASE step not depending on the broken step. Same root pattern independently confirmed via a corrupted (non-UTF8) owner marker: _read_owner_marker()'s `except OSError` does not catch UnicodeDecodeError (a ValueError subclass).
M123R-01.consequence: Exception still correctly surfaces (no false PASS, no cross-run damage) but 'resources cleaned up when possible' (the module's own section-5 promise) is violated -- a confirmed, reproducible resource leak in this narrow but real scenario.

M123R-02.title: Ownership mismatch causes futile full-budget rescue retry instead of immediate stop
M123R-02.consequence: No safety violation (other run's resources verified untouched throughout) -- but a structurally-undecidable-by-retry condition (caller passed mismatched run_root) is retried for the full RESCUE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS budget before correctly re-raising, wasting ~90s per occurrence.

TOCTOU_window_INFO.title: TOCTOU window exists between verify_ownership() and shutil.rmtree() in principle, not exploitable on this platform
TOCTOU_window_INFO.detail: Deterministic worst-case-timing hijack tested with both a symlink and a Windows junction (mklink /J) replacing the run root at the exact instant after ownership was confirmed. Both blocked completely by Python stdlib's shutil._rmtree_islink() (checks both S_ISLNK and IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT since Python 3.8+) -- victim directories survived fully intact in both tests. Not a finding; documented per the audit's own guidance not to require redesign for a non-realistically-exploitable local-harness risk.
